name: Football Analytics Hackathon
description:
The technological innovations of recent years - in particular, advances in the field of position tracking – lead to enormous amounts of data in soccer. In this module students will have to solve challenges given by an expert group including sport data scientists, professional soccer clubs and sports data companies. Students will be organized interdisciplinary workgroups including students students from computer science as well as from sport science. 

Challenges are related to soccer performance. The refer to an technical or tactical concept in soccer such as pressing, passing quality, line break, build up play, circle play, movements to receive, tactical formation, physical effort passing lines and much more. Based on these concepts the students will have to 
•	specify the concept from the perspective of sport science (e.g., what is pressing?) 
•	specify the concept from the perspective of computer science science (e.g., how can we model pressing in a mathematical way?) 
•	develop a technical solution for detecting this concept in raw data (e.g., identifying the timespans, in which pressing occurs). 
•	validate the detection quality based on video analysis (e.g., did you found the right timespans?). 
•	calculate performance indicators based on these concept (e.g. number of successful and non-successful pressing situations).  
•	use appropriate methods from visual analytics to make the numbers be interpretable in an easy and intuitive way (e.g. by visualizing indicators in relation to context variables). 
•	interpret the results from the perspective of performance analysis (e.g. ,how can the results be used by a coach?)
prerequisites: Background in performance analysis and/or machine learning/AI/computer Science. Bachelor degree
